Method of Attack: Encrypts files on the compromised machine and demands ransom for file decryption
Indicators of Compromise: Files will be encrypted and changed to have a ".darky" file extension.
A ransom note named "Restore-My-Files.txt" is deposited in locations where files are encrypted.

Method of Attack: Encrypts files on compromised machines and adds a file extension named after the target company to the affected files.
Indicators of Compromise: A unique file extension is appended to the affected files.
An MSI (Windows installer) file is used to deliver the ransomware.

Method of Attack: Encrypts files on a victim’s machine and demands a price for software to decrypt the affected files.
Indicators of Compromise: Files encrypted by vvyu will have a ".vvyu" file extension appended to them.
A ransom note is deposited in every location where files are encrypted.

Method of Attack: Encrypts files on a victim machine and demands a ransom.
Indicators of Compromise: Files will be encrypted and appended with a ".Kriptor" file extension.
A running clock will count down from 72 hours, after which point the malware authors threaten to double the ransom and/or prevent decryption permanently from that point onwards.

Method of Attack: Encrypts files on compromised machines and threatens to release a victim’s data on the Internet if they do not pay the requested ransom.
Indicators of Compromise: Files encrypted by Cuba will have a ".cuba" file extension appended.
A ransom note named "!! READ ME !!.txt" is deposited in any directory where files have been encrypted.
